cards.text: Jesus has just set free a woman who'd been hunched over for eighteen years, and the whole crowd rejoiced (Luke 13:10-17). Then He asks, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?” I love a teacher who asks a question and then answers it. Back in the drawer, NOBODY ever answered mine.

cards.question: Jesus picks something to compare the kingdom of God to. What does He reach for first?

cards.text: A mustard seed. A man tosses it into his garden, and when Matthew tells this same picture, it's the smallest of all seeds (Matthew 13:32).

cards.question: A man tosses a tiny mustard seed into his garden. What does it grow into?

cards.text: A TREE. From a seed so small it could get lost in my mustache, and friend, a LOT of things get lost in this mustache.

cards.question: The mustard seed has become a tree. What do the birds of the air do in its branches?

cards.text: Here, Jesus doesn't stop to explain the tree. He just asks again, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?”

cards.question: Jesus is about to give a second picture of the kingdom of God, and this one walks right into my bakery. What does He compare it to?

cards.text: LEAVEN! Jesus just walked into MY world, friend, and I'm trying to stay calm, but this mustache is already waving at the crowd.

cards.question: True or false: In Jesus' second picture, it's a man who takes the leaven and mixes it into the flour.
A woman mixes leaven into three measures of flour, until ___ of it is leavened.

cards.text: ALL of it. Leaven never stays in its corner, friend. It gets into every bit, the same way flour gets into my eyebrows and NEVER leaves.

cards.question: Look at both of Jesus' pictures of the kingdom of God, the mustard seed and the leaven. What happens to the thing that goes in?

answers.text: It ends up far bigger than it started
It gets lost and never shows up again
It gets pulled out and thrown away

cards.text: Two pictures of the kingdom of God: a seed that becomes a tree full of nests, and leaven worked through all the flour. I'm gonna think about this every time I mix a batch, and honestly, I mix a LOT of batches.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences, not counting the second sentence inside the quote: the setup about the healed woman, the quote line, "I love a teacher who asks a question and then answers it," and "Back in the drawer, NOBODY ever answered mine." That is more than the limit for the opening card.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer the baker just gave ("A TREE") and adds a mustache joke. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke has nothing in the passage to ride on.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question's setup says the second picture "walks right into my bakery." That points to a baking ingredient, which rules out the wrong answers Salt and Honey and leaves Leaven as the only bakery fit.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to the answer just given ("LEAVEN!") with a joke about Jesus walking into his world and his mustache waving. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move it forward. It also repeats the "walked into my bakery" idea from card 8.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "ALL of it." / "Leaven never stays in its corner, friend." / "It gets into every bit..." That is more than the limit for a story card after the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question covers both pictures, but the right answer "It ends up far bigger than it started" is only true for the mustard seed. Luke 13:21 says the leaven is mixed in until all the flour is leavened. It never says the leaven grows bigger. The answer stretches the text for the leaven.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both.

findings.problem: The last story card restates both pictures already covered, the seed that becomes a tree full of nests and the leaven worked through all the flour, and adds a closing joke. It tells nothing new from the passage, so it works as a recap card.
Five of the seven choice cards are multiple choice, with one true or false and one fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
